# Species contributions (Q4)

**What and why.** The observed movement of a community between t1 and t2 is the sum of one
vector per species: the change in the species' share times the species' fixed position in the
CCA plane. Projecting each species' vector on a reference direction says how much that species
moved the community along it. Two measures are used, both per century. Along the direction the
prediction moved (`contrib_climate`), a positive value means the species carried the community with
the climate. The second measure, `contrib_lag`, splits the lag rate itself. The mismatch g, from the
predicted to the observed position, is taken at both ends (g1 at t1, g2 at t2), and m is their sum
divided by the sum of their lengths. Each species' vector projected on m is that species' part of the
lag rate, and the predicted movement projected on m, with its sign reversed, is the climate's part.
Because the change in mismatch, g2 − g1, is the observed movement minus the predicted movement, and
(g2 − g1)·m is exactly the change in the length of the mismatch, the species parts and the climate
part add up exactly to the lag rate (asserted). A negative species value means the species narrowed
the lag, a positive value that it widened it. Swapping the two surveys reverses every value, so the
measure has no direction of its own. It replaces `contrib_gap`, the projection on the mismatch at
the start alone. That measure leaned positive: a community sampled away from its predicted position
tends to come back towards it by chance, and run backwards in time it also appeared to close the
gap. `contrib_lag` is per century of the same interval as the lag rate.

**How it is calculated.**

```{r step6-code}
code_snippet('R/helpers/cca_transition_contributions.R', 'contrib-lag')
code_snippet('R/pipeline/15_contributions.R', 'species-means')
```

**Result.**

```{r step6-results}
species_means = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means.csv')
species_means |> mutate(value = ifelse(interval_defined, sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
    ifelse(present, sprintf('%+.3f', estimate), 'absent'))) |>
  select(measure, species, site, period_type, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, period_type), values_from = value) |>
  rename(Species = species, Park = site) |>
  show_table('step6_species_means', caption = paste('**Species contributions**, mean and 95% t-interval in CCA',
    'distance per century, per species, park and period type. Columns: measure (contrib_climate along the',
    'predicted movement, contrib_lag the species\' part of the lag rate) and period type. "absent": the species',
    'does not occur in that park and period type. contrib_lag includes the units where the community did not',
    'move (all species values zero), contrib_climate does not (epsilon rule).'))
lag_parts = read_output('cca_transition_contributions/lag_decomposition.csv')
tci = function(x) { n = length(x); m = mean(x); h = qt(.975, n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n)
  sprintf('%+.3f (%+.3f to %+.3f)', m, m - h, m + h) }
lag_parts |> mutate(period_type = factor(period_type, levels = c('Holocene-S', 'Holocene-C', 'Anthropocene'))) |>
  group_by(Park = site, `Period type` = period_type) |>
  summarise(Units = n(), `Lag rate` = tci(lag_rate), `Species (sum)` = tci(species_sum),
    `Climate part` = tci(climate_part), .groups = 'drop') |>
  show_table('step6_lag_decomposition', caption = paste('**The lag rate split into the species and the climate.**',
    'Plain means over the lake-periods or plot pairs with 95% t-intervals, in CCA distance per century. In',
    'every unit the sum over species plus the climate part equals the lag rate. Positive values widen the lag.'))
```

The species vectors add up to the observed movement for every lake-period and plot pair (asserted).
```{r step6-numbers}
hol = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene')
hol_away = hol |> filter(interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
lag_species = species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene', measure == 'contrib_lag', interval_defined)
lp = lag_parts |> filter(era == 'Anthropocene') |> group_by(site) |>
  summarise(lag = mean(lag_rate), species = mean(species_sum), climate = mean(climate_part))
lpv = function(p, v) sprintf('%+.2f', lp[[v]][lp$site == p])
narrow = lag_species |> filter(conf_high < 0); widen = lag_species |> filter(conf_low > 0)
r_measures = species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene') |>
  select(measure, species, site, estimate) |> pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = estimate) |>
  group_by(site) |> summarise(r = cor(contrib_climate, contrib_lag, use = 'complete.obs'))
```

In the Holocene every species mean is close to zero in both parks (largest absolute value
`r sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(hol$estimate)))` CCA distance per century).
`r nrow(hol_away)` of `r sum(hol$interval_defined)` Holocene intervals exclude zero
(`r paste(sprintf('%s, %s, %s, %s', hol_away$species, hol_away$site, hol_away$period_type, hol_away$measure), collapse = '; ')`),
all smaller than `r sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(hol_away$estimate)))` in absolute value. The Anthropocene
means are larger.

In the Anthropocene the climate's part of the lag rate is about the same in both parks
(`r lpv('MORA', 'climate')` at MORA, `r lpv('NOCA', 'climate')` at NOCA, CCA distance per century): the
predicted positions moved away from the communities. The parks differ in their species. At MORA the
species added to the lag (sum `r lpv('MORA', 'species')`), so the lag rate was `r lpv('MORA', 'lag')`. At
NOCA they narrowed it by more than the climate widened it (sum `r lpv('NOCA', 'species')`), so the lag
rate was `r lpv('NOCA', 'lag')`. Species whose interval lies below zero, which narrowed the lag:
`r paste(sprintf('%s (%s, %+.3f)', narrow$species, narrow$site, narrow$estimate), collapse = ', ')`.
Species whose interval lies above zero, which widened it:
`r paste(sprintf('%s (%s, %+.3f)', widen$species, widen$site, widen$estimate), collapse = ', ')`.
Across species the two measures are negatively correlated in the Anthropocene
(r = `r sprintf('%.2f', r_measures$r[r_measures$site == 'MORA'])` at MORA,
`r sprintf('%.2f', r_measures$r[r_measures$site == 'NOCA'])` at NOCA): species that moved the community with the
climate-predicted direction narrowed the lag, and those that moved it against that direction widened
it.

```{r step6-contrasts}
sc = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_contrasts.csv')
sc_sig = sc |> filter(p_adjusted < .05)
```

The period types of a species are compared with Welch tests, three contrasts per species, measure and
park, and the p-values are Holm-adjusted within each measure and park across all species and
contrasts. Of `r sum(!is.na(sc$p_value))` testable contrasts, `r sum(sc$p_value < .05, na.rm = TRUE)` have
p < 0.05 before the adjustment and `r nrow(sc_sig)` after it
(`r paste(sprintf('%s %s, %s, %s', sc_sig$species, sc_sig$site, sc_sig$contrast, sc_sig$measure), collapse = '; ')`).
`r if (nrow(sc_sig) && all(startsWith(sc_sig$contrast, 'Anthropocene'))) 'All of them set the Anthropocene against a Holocene period type.' else ''`

```{r fig-8-main}
show_figure('report/figures/main/fig_species_contributions.pdf')
```

**Figure 8. Species contributions in the Holocene and the Anthropocene.** Each species' vector is its
change in share between the first and the last sampled century of a lake-period, or between the
legacy survey and the resurvey of a plot, times its fixed position in the CCA plane. The upper row (following climate-predicted direction)
projects these vectors on the direction in which the climate-predicted position moved, and the lower
row (changing the climate-community lag) on the average direction of the mismatch at the two ends, so
that the species' values plus the climate's part add up to the lag rate. Labels at the top of each panel read with the row title: a species moved the community following or against the climate-predicted direction (upper row), and narrowed or widened the climate-community lag (lower row). The lower row includes the lake-periods and plot pairs whose composition did not change (all species values zero) and is per century of the same interval as the lag rate.
Species are ordered by the maximum elevation of the plots where they occur (the 605 plot pairs, both surveys, both parks), the highest at the top. Their names are shaded by that maximum in four grey steps, lightest below 1,500 m and black above 1,900 m (key below the figure). Names in bold are species absent from the Holocene record of both parks.
Symbols are means: triangles, Holocene stability periods, circles, Holocene climate-change periods,
diamonds, Anthropocene plot pairs (burned and unburned together). Large symbols with bars are means whose
95% t-interval excludes zero, small faded symbols are means whose interval includes zero. A species with no
Holocene symbols in a park is absent from that park's Holocene record.
Each park has its own x scale, symmetric around zero. `r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance per century.

**Check: species contributions not divided by time.** Per century, the Holocene species values are
small partly because the lake-periods are long, and the Anthropocene values are large partly because the
plot pairs are short.

```{r step6-totals}
st = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means_total.csv')
stc = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_contrasts_total.csv')
dts = read_output('cca_transition_contributions/species_contributions.csv') |>
  distinct(era, site, series, unit_index, plot_id, vegetation_dt_years) |>
  group_by(era) |> summarise(lo = min(vegetation_dt_years), hi = max(vegetation_dt_years))
dr = function(e) sprintf('%s to %s', prettyNum(dts$lo[dts$era == e], big.mark = ','),
  prettyNum(dts$hi[dts$era == e], big.mark = ','))
# Means whose 95% interval excludes zero, for species present in that park and period type.
away = function(d) d |> filter(present, interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
key = function(d) sort(paste(d$measure, d$species, d$site))
hol_t = st |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
hol_r = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
top = hol_t |> slice_max(abs(estimate), n = 1)
ant_t = away(st |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
ant_r = away(species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS15_species_contributions_total.pdf')
```

The Holocene lake-periods span `r dr('Holocene')` years and the Anthropocene plot pairs `r dr('Anthropocene')`
years. Fig. S15 shows the species means without dividing by time, that is how far each species moved the
community over the whole lake-period or plot pair. The Holocene means then reach the size of the
Anthropocene ones (largest *`r top$species`* at `r top$site`, `r top$period_type`, `r top$measure`,
`r sprintf('%+.3f', top$estimate)` CCA distance), but they vary so much between the few lake-periods that
`r nrow(away(hol_t))` of `r sum(hol_t$interval_defined)` Holocene intervals exclude zero, against
`r nrow(away(hol_r))` per century. In the Anthropocene `r nrow(ant_t)` means exclude zero, against
`r nrow(ant_r)` per century, `r if (identical(key(ant_t), key(ant_r))) 'the same species in the same parks' else 'not all the same species'`.
After the Holm adjustment `r sum(stc$p_adjusted < .05, na.rm = TRUE)` of `r sum(!is.na(stc$p_value))`
contrasts between period types are significant, against `r nrow(sc_sig)` per century. The large
Anthropocene species rates therefore come mainly from changes made within a few decades. Over a whole
lake-period, Holocene species moved the community about as far, but too variably to say which species did.

**Fig. S15. Species contributions not divided by time.** As Figure 8, with each species' contribution
taken over the whole lake-period or plot pair instead of per century. Upper row: the distance the species
moved the community along the direction in which the climate-predicted position moved. Lower row: the
species' part of the change in mismatch between the two ends, so that the species' values plus the
climate's part add up to the lag. Plain means with 95% t-intervals, symbols, order and shading as in
Figure 8. `r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance.

# Appendix S3. Bias-corrected paleoclimate

```{r appendix-s3-setup}
s3_dir = here::here('output_bias_corrected', 'comparison')
s3_has = file.exists(file.path(s3_dir, 'explanatory_slopes_raw_vs_corrected.csv'))
s3_bias = read_output('chelsa_paleo_bias_correction.csv')
s3_term_label = c(siteNOCA = 'Site (NOCA minus MORA)', climate_rate = 'Climate change rate',
  climate_change = 'Climate change', fire_activity = 'Fire activity')
s3_p = function(p) ifelse(p < .001, '< 0.001', sprintf('%.3f', p))
s3_rng = function(v, col) sprintf('%+.1f to %+.1f', min(s3_bias[[col]][s3_bias$variable == v]), max(s3_bias[[col]][s3_bias$variable == v]))
```

**What and why.** The Holocene climate-predicted positions come from CHELSA-TraCE21k, while the CCA is
calibrated on CHELSA V2.1. Over the period both products cover, they differ at each lake. Depending on
the lake and the month, the modern CHELSA-TraCE21k slice differs from the 1979 to 2021 CHELSA V2.1 mean by
`r s3_rng('tasmax', 'add_offset')` °C in maximum temperature and `r s3_rng('tasmin', 'add_offset')` °C in minimum
temperature, and CHELSA V2.1 has `r sprintf('%.1f to %.1f', min(s3_bias$mul_factor, na.rm = TRUE), max(s3_bias$mul_factor, na.rm = TRUE))`
times its precipitation. A difference of this kind shifts every climate-predicted position of a lake, and
with it the mismatch at both ends of a lake-period. All Holocene analyses were therefore repeated with the
difference removed, by a fixed offset per lake and month for temperature and a fixed ratio for
precipitation: [`R/sensitivity_bias_corrected.R`](R/sensitivity_bias_corrected.R) reruns stages 07 to 15
with `PALEO_USE_BIAS_CORRECTED = TRUE` into `output_bias_corrected/` and leaves the primary outputs
untouched. The climate periods stay those of the raw series, so the same lake-periods are compared. The
observed positions do not change, and therefore neither do the turnover, the displacement and the
Anthropocene values.

```{r appendix-s3-figure}
if (s3_has) {
  s3_lp = readr::read_csv(file.path(s3_dir, 'lake_period_responses_raw_vs_corrected.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    filter(is.finite(raw), is.finite(corrected))
  s3_kept = function(r, p = c('MORA', 'NOCA')) { x = s3_lp |> filter(response == r, site %in% p)
    sprintf('%d of %d', sum(sign(x$raw) == sign(x$corrected)), nrow(x)) }
  s3_cc = s3_lp |> filter(response == 'climate_change', raw > 0)
  s3_ec = readr::read_csv(file.path(s3_dir, 'era_contrasts_raw_vs_corrected.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(sig_raw = p_adjusted_raw < .05, sig_corrected = p_adjusted_corrected < .05)
  s3_ec_changed = s3_ec |> filter(sig_raw != sig_corrected)
  s3_sl = readr::read_csv(file.path(s3_dir, 'explanatory_slopes_raw_vs_corrected.csv'), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(away_raw = conf_low_raw > 0 | conf_high_raw < 0, away_corrected = conf_low_corrected > 0 | conf_high_corrected < 0)
  s3_sl_changed = s3_sl |> filter(away_raw != away_corrected)
  show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS16_bias_correction_lake_periods.pdf', width = '75%')
} else cat('Run Rscript R/sensitivity_bias_corrected.R to fill this appendix.\n')
```

**Fig. S16. Holocene lake-periods with the raw and the bias-corrected paleoclimate.** Each point is one
lake-period, with its value from the raw paleoclimate (x) against its value from the bias-corrected
paleoclimate (y): (A) climate change and (B) its rate, (C) the lag and (D) its rate, (E) the pace effect
and (F) its rate, (G) the direction effect and (H) its rate. Totals over the lake-period on the left,
rates per century on the right. Blue MORA, orange NOCA, triangles Holocene stability periods, circles
Holocene climate-change periods. On the dashed line the correction changes nothing. In the shaded
quadrants the value changes sign. Lake-periods whose observed or predicted position did not move have no
pace or direction effect. Turnover and displacement are the same in both runs and are not shown. Climate
change in standardized units, the other quantities in CCA distance (totals) or CCA distance per century
(rates). Script: [`R/figures/supp_bias_correction.R`](R/figures/supp_bias_correction.R).

```{r appendix-s3-text, results = 'asis'}
if (s3_has) {
  s3_lst = function(d, f) if (nrow(d)) paste(f(d), collapse = '; ') else 'none'
  cat(paste0('**Result.** The correction changes the climate change of a lake-period by a median of ',
    sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * median(abs(s3_cc$corrected / s3_cc$raw - 1))), ' (Fig. S16A, B). It changes the sign of many ',
    'lags. The lag keeps its sign in ', s3_kept('lag', 'MORA'), ' lake-periods at MORA and ', s3_kept('lag', 'NOCA'),
    ' at NOCA, the pace effect in ', s3_kept('pace_effect_total', 'MORA'), ' and ', s3_kept('pace_effect_total', 'NOCA'),
    ', and the direction effect in ', s3_kept('direction_effect_total', 'MORA'), ' and ',
    s3_kept('direction_effect_total', 'NOCA'), ' (the rates share the sign of the totals). The MORA Holocene lags are ',
    'small, so a small shift in the two mismatches is enough to flip them. Of the ', nrow(s3_ec), ' era contrasts (Table S3.1), ',
    sum(s3_ec$sig_raw), ' are significant after the Holm adjustment with the raw paleoclimate and ', sum(s3_ec$sig_corrected),
    ' with the bias-corrected one. Those whose significance differs between the runs: ',
    s3_lst(s3_ec_changed, function(d) sprintf('%s, %s, %s (Holm p %s raw, %s corrected)', response_label[d$response], d$site,
      d$contrast, s3_p(d$p_adjusted_raw), s3_p(d$p_adjusted_corrected))), '. Of the ', nrow(s3_sl), ' Holocene explanatory slopes ',
    '(Table S3.2), ', sum(s3_sl$away_raw), ' have an interval that excludes zero with the raw paleoclimate and ',
    sum(s3_sl$away_corrected), ' with the bias-corrected one. Those that differ: ',
    s3_lst(s3_sl_changed, function(d) sprintf('%s, %s', response_label[d$response], s3_term_label[d$term])), '.\n'))
}
```

```{r appendix-s3-contrasts}
s3_ci = function(e, lo, hi) sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', e, lo, hi)
if (s3_has) {

}
```

```{r numbers-step0}
    `MORA lake-centuries outside (%)` = 100 * first(extrapolated_share_MORA),
    `NOCA lake-centuries outside (%)` = 100 * first(extrapolated_share_NOCA)) |>
  show_table('numbers_step0', caption = paste0('**Screening.** Adding MWT and WP to MSpT + SP: pseudo-F ',
    sprintf('%.2f', addback$pseudo_F[1]), ', p = ', sprintf('%.4f', addback$p_value[addback$design == 'Unrestricted']),
    ' unrestricted and ', sprintf('%.4f', addback$p_value[addback$design == 'Within parks']), ' within parks.'))
```

**Climate periods and lake-periods.**

```{r numbers-units}
units |> group_by(Park = site, `Period type` = period_type) |>
  summarise(`Lake-periods` = n(), `Years (min)` = min(duration_yr), `Years (max)` = max(duration_yr),
    `Climate change rate (mean)` = mean(climate_rate), `Fire activity (min)` = min(fire_activity),
    `Fire activity (max)` = max(fire_activity), `Fire activity (mean)` = mean(fire_activity), .groups = 'drop') |>
  show_table('numbers_units', caption = sprintf(paste('**Lake-periods** (raw values, not model estimates). %d lake and',
    'period combinations had a sampled century, and %d had two or more.'), nrow(candidates), nrow(units)))
```

**Climate–community lags, pace and direction: era models, fitted means, contrasts and folds per park.**

```{r numbers-era}
means |> transmute(Response = response_label[response], Park = site, `Period type` = period_type, n,
    Mean = f2(estimate), `95% CI` = ci(conf_low, conf_high)) |>
  show_table('numbers_era_means', caption = '**Fitted means.**')
contrasts |> transmute(Response = response_label[response], Park = site, Contrast = contrast,
    Estimate = f2(estimate), `95% CI` = ci(conf_low, conf_high), p = p_value, `p (Holm)` = p_adjusted) |>
  show_table('numbers_era_contrasts', caption = paste('**Contrasts between period types.** p (Holm) is adjusted',
    'across the six contrasts of each response (three per park). Quote the adjusted p.'))
folds |> transmute(Response = response_label[response], Park = site, `Anthropocene over` = against, Fold = fold) |>
  show_table('numbers_era_folds', caption = '**Folds.** The Holocene-C fold is the one quoted as a speed.')
```

**Associations with fire: Holocene explanatory models and their Anthropocene counterpart.**

```{r numbers-step5}
coefficients |> filter(term != '(Intercept)') |>
  transmute(Response = label[metric], Era = era, Term = term, Estimate = f2(estimate),
    `95% CI` = ci(conf_low, conf_high), p = p_value) |>
  show_table('numbers_step5', caption = paste('**Slopes and contrasts.** Climate change rate: per standardized unit per',
    'century. Fire activity: per event per century per covered core. Each model has one group contrast (site, and',
    'burned minus unburned in the Anthropocene), so these p-values need no adjustment for multiple contrasts.'))
```

**Species contributions.**

```{r numbers-step6}
species_means |> filter(interval_defined) |>
  group_by(Measure = measure, Park = site, `Period type` = period_type) |>
  summarise(Species = n(), `Interval above zero` = sum(conf_low > 0), `Interval below zero` = sum(conf_high < 0),
    `Largest absolute mean` = max(abs(estimate)), .groups = 'drop') |>
  show_table('numbers_step6', caption = '**Species means** per measure, park and period type (species with a defined interval).')
```

**Figure 3, climate rates.**

```{r numbers-fig2}
read_output('figures/holocene_climate_level_rates.csv') |>
  transmute(Kind = kind, Variable = variable, Period = coalesce(period, ''), `cal BP` = t, `Rate per century` = rate) |>
  bind_rows(rates2 |> transmute(Kind = 'Anthropocene plot median', Variable = variable, Period = site,
    `Rate per century` = rate)) |>
  show_table('numbers_fig2', caption = '**Real-unit climate rates per century** (°C for MSpT, mm for SP).')
```

**Doubts the paper must face (`PLAN.md` section 9), with the numbers that bear on them.**

```{r numbers-doubts}
fire_by = units |> group_by(site, period_type) |> summarise(mean = mean(fire_activity), .groups = 'drop')
fire_slope = coefficients |> filter(era == 'Holocene', term == 'fire_activity')
tibble(Doubt = c(
  'MORA fire comes from Sunrise Ridge, the vegetation lakes lie elsewhere',
  'Fire values of the two parks barely overlap',
  'Within MORA the stability periods sat at the lowest fire values',
  'Rates over about 29 years and over centuries are not on equal footing',
  'MSpT + SP must be argued on mechanism'),
  Numbers = c(
    paste(sprintf('%s fire slope %s (%s)', label[fire_slope$metric], f2(fire_slope$estimate), ci(fire_slope$conf_low, fire_slope$conf_high)), collapse = '; '),
    paste(sprintf('%s %.2f to %.2f', c('MORA', 'NOCA'), tapply(units$fire_activity, units$site, min),
      tapply(units$fire_activity, units$site, max)), collapse = ', '),
    paste(sprintf('%s %s mean %.3f', fire_by$site, fire_by$period_type, fire_by$mean), collapse = ', '),
    both_spans,
    sprintf('Adjusted R² %.3f with MSpT + SP against %.3f with all four. Adding MWT and WP: p = %.4f unrestricted, %.4f within parks.',
      screening$adjusted_R2[screening$set == 'MSpT + SP'][1], screening$adjusted_R2[screening$set == 'All four'][1],
      addback$p_value[addback$design == 'Unrestricted'], addback$p_value[addback$design == 'Within parks']))) |>
  show_table('numbers_doubts', caption = '**Doubts and the numbers that bear on them.**')
```
